value.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
value.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
value.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

value.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
value.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
value.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

value.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
value.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
value.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

value.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
value.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
value.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

value.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
value.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
value.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

value.zh: 十二月，吳夏口督、前將軍孫秀帥眾來奔，拜驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，封會稽公。
value.en: In the twelfth month: Sun Xiu, Wu’s Xiakou commander, defected with his army and received a ducal title and swift-cavalry command.
value.literal: In the twelfth month Sun Xiu, Wu’s commander at Xiakou and former forward general, led his troops to defect; he was appointed general of swift cavalry with independent command equal to the three excellencies and enfeoffed as duke of Kuaiji.

value.zh: 戊辰，復置鎮軍官。
value.en: On wuchen the “guard the army” office was revived.
value.literal: On the day wuchen the post of general who guards the army was restored.

value.zh: 三月，孫皓帥眾趨壽陽，遣大司馬望屯淮北以距之。
value.en: Third month: Sun Hao marched on Shouyang; grand marshal Sima Wang took station north of the Huai to meet him.
value.literal: In the third month Sun Hao led his host toward Shouyang; the grand marshal Wang was sent to encamp north of the Huai to block him.

value.zh: 丙戌，司空、鉅鹿公裴秀薨。
value.en: On bingxu [13] Pei Xiu, minister of works, died.
value.literal: On the day bingxu [13] Pei Xiu, minister of works and duke of Julu, died.

value.zh: 癸巳，以中護軍王業爲尚書左僕射，高陽王珪爲尚書右僕射。
value.en: Guisi: Wang Ye, Central Protector of the Army, was made left vice-director of the Secretariat, and Sima Gui, King of Gaoyang, was made right vice-director of the Secretariat.
value.literal: On the day guisi Wang Ye, central protector, was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the left, and king Gui of Gaoyang senior vice-director of the masters of the right.

value.zh: 孫秀部將何崇帥眾五千人來降。
value.en: Sun Xiu’s officer He Chong brought five thousand soldiers over to Jin.
value.literal: He Chong, a subordinate general under Sun Xiu, led five thousand men to surrender.

value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 武帝泰始四年七月，星隕如雨，皆西流。
value.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, stars fell like rain, all streaming westward.
value.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, stars fell like rain, all streaming westward.

value.zh: 占曰：「星隕為百姓叛。
value.en: The prognostication said, "Falling stars mean the common people rebel.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Star falls mean commoners rebel.

value.zh: 西流，吳人歸晉之象也。」
value.en: Flowing west is the image of the people of Wu returning to Jin."
value.literal: Westward flow meant Wu men submitting to Jin.

value.zh: 二年，吳夏口督孫秀率部曲二千餘人來降。
value.en: Sun Xiu defected to Jin.
value.literal: In the second year Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led more than two thousand retainers (buqu) to defect.

value.zh: 昔者元胎無象，太素流形，對越在天，以爲元首，則記所謂冬居營窟，夏居橧巢，飲血茹毛，未有麻絲者也。
value.en: In the earliest age, before form coalesced from undivided simplicity, people already looked toward heaven as their sovereign; the old annals picture them wintering in earthen dens, summering in treetop huts, living on raw flesh and blood, long before cloth ever softened their lives.
value.literal: In antiquity the primordial embryo had no image; Grand Simplicity flowed into forms; facing and answering what is on high, they took it as the supreme head—then the records say they dwelt in burrows in winter and nests in summer, drank blood and ate fur, and had not yet hemp or silk.

value.zh: 及燧人鑽火，庖犧出震，風宗下武，炎胤昌基，畫野無聞，其歸一揆。
value.en: Then Suiren struck fire from wood, Fuxi rose in the east like thunder, wind and flame passed their line down to martial kings, and the royal house widened its base; we hear nothing yet of surveying fields into squares, but every step still aimed at the same single standard of rule.
value.literal: When Suiren drilled fire, Paoxi emerged in the Zhen (east) trigram; the Feng lineage descended to the martial kings, and the Yan heirs broadened the foundation; dividing the wilds is not heard of—their return is one measure.

value.zh: 黃帝則東海南江，登空躡岱，至於崑峰振轡，崆山訪道，[1]存諸汗竹，不可厚誣。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor pressed east to the sea and south along the great streams, climbed Kongsang and crossed Mount Tai, climbed Kunlun to tighten his reins and sought the Way on Kongshan; the fact is inked on bamboo that has soaked in human sweat, and it would be perverse to dismiss it as mere legend.
value.literal: As for the Yellow Emperor: east to the sea, south to the great rivers; ascending hollow (Kong) and treading Dai; reaching Kun peaks to shake the reins, Kongshan to inquire of the Way—[1] it is preserved on sweating bamboo strips and cannot be heavily slandered.

value.zh: 高陽任地依神，帝嚳順天行義。
value.en: Zhuanxu, the High Yang line, grounded his power in the land and the spirits; Emperor Ku shaped policy by heaven's pattern and the moral law.
value.literal: Gaoyang relied on earth and depended on spirits; Emperor Ku followed heaven and practiced righteousness.

value.zh: 東踰蟠木，西濟流沙，北至幽陵，南撫交阯，日月所經，舟車所至，莫匪王臣，不踰茲域。
value.en: Their sway ran east past the curling forest, west across the shifting sands, north to the cold marches, south to the Red River delta—every place the sun and moon lit and every road a wheel could find lay inside the ring of royal subjects, and nothing beyond that ring counted as theirs.
value.literal: East they crossed Panmu, west they forded the flowing sands, north they reached Youling, south they soothed Jiaozhi; wherever sun and moon passed, wherever boat and cart could reach, none were not the king's subjects—they did not overstep this domain.

value.zh: 帝堯時，禹平水土，以爲九州。
value.en: Under Emperor Yao, Yu drained the flood and settled the soil, and from that labor the Nine Provinces took their shape.
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Yao, Yu pacified the waters and earth, and thereby made the nine provinces.

value.zh: 虞舜登庸，厥功彌劭，表提類而分區宇，判山河而考疆域，冀北創并部之名，燕齊起幽營之號，則書所謂肇十有二州，封十有二山者也。
value.en: Once Shun took office, his achievement only deepened: he sorted kinds of terrain, carved the realm into regions, traced ranges and rivers to fix true borders, split the northern Ji plain to name the Bing command, and gave Yan and Qi the new titles of You and Ying—exactly the twelve provinces and twelve sacred peaks the classics say he first ordained.
value.literal: When Shun of Yu ascended to employment, his merit grew ever greater; he displayed categories and divided the regional cosmos, adjudicated mountains and rivers and examined boundaries; north of Ji he created the name of the Bing department; in Yan and Qi he raised the designations of You and Ying—this is what the documents call initiating twelve provinces and enfeoffing twelve mountains.

value.zh: 夏功在于唐堯，殷因無所損益。
value.en: The Xia built on the work of Yao of Tang; the Shang inherited that map and left its proportions unchanged.
value.literal: The Xia's achievement lay in Tang-Yao; the Yin inherited and had nothing to diminish or increase.

value.zh: 周武克商，自豐徂鎬。
value.en: When King Wu of Zhou overthrew the Shang, he moved the seat of power from Feng to Hao.
value.literal: King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, from Feng going to Hao.

value.zh: 至成王時，改作禹貢，徐梁入於青雍，冀野析於幽并。
value.en: Under King Cheng the court rewrote the "Tribute of Yu" grid: Xu and Liang were folded into Qing and Yong, while the old Ji heartland was carved into new You and Bing sectors.
value.literal: By the time of King Cheng, they revised and made the Tribute of Yu; Xu and Liang were absorbed into Qing and Yong; the wilds of Ji were split into You and Bing.

value.zh: 職方掌天下之土，以周厥利；
value.en: The Bureau of Domains held the register of every soil under heaven, weighing what each tract could yield;
value.literal: The Office of Regions grasped the soil of all under heaven, in order to complete its advantages;

value.zh: 保章辯九州之野，皆有分星。
value.en: The star-masters matched each of the Nine Provinces to its own stretch of sky, every region with its allotted constellation.
value.literal: The Star-Clerk distinguished the wilds of the nine provinces; each had apportioned stars.

value.zh: 東南曰揚州，正南曰荊州，河南曰豫州，正東曰青州，河東曰兗州，正西曰雍州，東北曰幽州，河內曰冀州，正北曰并州。
value.en: The southeast quarter was Yangzhou, the south face Jingzhou, the ground south of the Yellow River Yuzhou, the east face Qingzhou, the ground east of the river Yanzhou, the west face Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, the inner bend of the river Jizhou, and the north face Bingzhou.
value.literal: The southeast is called Yangzhou, the due south Jingzhou, south of the river Yuzhou, the due east Qingzhou, east of the river Yanzhou, the due west Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, within the river Jizhou, the due north Bingzhou.

value.zh: 始皇初并天下，懲{乂心}戰國，削罷列侯，分天下爲三十六郡。
value.en: The First Emperor, fresh from unifying the realm and determined not to repeat Warring States chaos, stripped the old enfeoffed nobles of power and carved the empire into thirty-six commanderies.
value.literal: When the First Emperor first united all under heaven, chastened by the Warring States, he cut away and abolished the ranked feudal lords and divided all under heaven into thirty-six commanderies.

value.zh: 〈三川、河東、南陽、南郡、九江、鄣郡、會稽、潁川、碭郡、泗水、薛郡、東郡、琅邪、齊郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西、遼東、代郡、鉅鹿、邯鄲、上黨、太原、雲中、九原、雁門、上郡、隴西、北地、漢中、巴郡、蜀郡、黔中、長沙，凡三十五郡，與內史爲三十六郡也。〉
value.en: 〈The thirty-five commanderies were Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, Xue, Dong, Langye, Qi, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba, Shu, Qianzhong, and Changsha; together with the metropolitan intendant's district, they made thirty-six commanderies.〉
value.literal: 〈Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang commandery, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang commandery, Sishui, Xue commandery, Dong commandery, Langye, Qi commandery, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai commandery, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang commandery, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba commandery, Shu commandery, Qianzhong, Changsha—in all thirty-five commanderies, which together with the metropolitan intendant made thirty-six commanderies.〉

value.zh: 於是興師踰江，平取百越，又置閩中、南海、桂林、象郡，凡四十郡，郡一守焉。
value.en: He then sent armies south of the Yangtze, crushed the Yue peoples, and added Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang, bringing the whole system to forty commanderies, each overseen by a single appointed governor.
value.literal: Thereupon they raised armies and crossed the rivers, pacified and took the Hundred Yue, and further established Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies—in all forty commanderies, each commandery having one governor.

value.zh: 其地則西臨洮而北沙漠，東縈西帶，皆臨大海。
value.en: The new realm ran west to the Tao River and north to the sands, while east and south it looped like a sash until every outer edge touched the sea.
value.literal: As for the territory: west it bordered Tao and north the desert; east winding, west belting—all bordered the great sea.

value.zh: 漢祖龍興，革秦之弊，分內史爲三部，更置郡國二十有三，
value.en: When the Han founder seized the mandate, he undid Qin's excesses, split the old inner intendant into three metropolitan circuits, and added twenty-three new commanderies and princely kingdoms,
value.literal: The Han progenitor rose like a dragon, reformed the Qin's abuses, divided the metropolitan intendant into three parts, and further established twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,

value.zh: 〈桂陽、江夏、豫章、河內、魏郡、東海、楚國、平原、梁國、定襄、泰山、汝南、淮陽、千乘、東萊、燕國、清河、信都、常山、中山、渤海、廣漢、涿郡，合二十三也。
value.en: 〈These were Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei, Donghai, Chu, Pingyuan, Liang, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, and Zhuo, twenty-three in all.
value.literal: 〈Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei commandery, Donghai, Chu kingdom, Pingyuan, Liang kingdom, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan kingdom, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, Zhuo commandery—together twenty-three.

value.zh: 三內史者，河上、渭南、中地也。
value.en: The three inner districts were Heshang south of the bend, Weinan, and the central capital belt.
value.literal: The three metropolitan intendants are: Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi.

value.zh: 地理志曰：高祖增二十六，武帝改河上、渭南、中地以爲京兆、馮翊、扶風，是爲三輔也。〉
value.en: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—these are the Three Adjuncts.〉
value.literal: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—this is the Three Adjuncts.〉

value.zh: 文增厥九，
value.en: Emperor Wen of Han added nine more,
value.literal: Wen added thereto nine,

value.zh: 〈廣平、城陽、淄川、濟南、膠西、膠東、河間、廬江、衡山，武帝改衡山曰「六安」。〉
value.en: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, and Hengshan—the last of which Emperor Wu renamed "Liu'an."〉
value.literal: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, Hengshan—Emperor Wu changed Hengshan to "Liu'an."〉

value.zh: 景加其四。
value.en: Emperor Jing added four more.
value.literal: Jing added four of them.

value.zh: 〈濟北、濟陰、山陽、北海也。
value.en: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.
value.literal: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.

value.zh: 宣改濟北曰東平。〉
value.en: Emperor Xuan renamed Jibei as Dongping.〉
value.literal: Xuan changed Jibei to Dongping.〉

value.zh: 武帝開越攘胡，初置十七，
value.en: Emperor Wu campaigned south against Yue and north against the steppe peoples, and his first expansion added seventeen commanderies,
value.literal: Emperor Wu opened the Yue and pushed back the Hu, at first establishing seventeen,

value.zh: 〈南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡，平西南夷置牂柯、越巂、沈黎、汶山、犍爲、益州六郡，西置武都郡，又分立零陵郡，合十七郡。〉
value.en: 〈nine southern coast commands from Nanhai to Dan'er, six carved from the southwest Yi heartland, Wudu on the western flank, and a split Lingling—seventeen new units in that push.〉
value.literal: 〈Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, Dan'er—nine commanderies; pacifying the southwestern Yi, established Zangke, Yuexi, Chenli, Wenshan, Qianwei, Yizhou—six commanderies; west established Wudu commandery; again separately established Lingling commandery—together seventeen commanderies.〉

value.zh: 拓土分疆，又增十四。
value.en: Further conquests widened the map by fourteen more commanderies.
value.literal: Expanding soil and dividing boundaries, again added fourteen.

value.zh: 〈弘農、臨淮、西河、朔方、酒泉、陳留、安定、天水、玄菟、樂浪、廣陵、敦煌、武威、張掖。〉
value.en: 〈The fourteen interior and frontier commanderies were Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, and Zhangye.〉
value.literal: 〈Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, Zhangye.〉

value.zh: 昭帝少事，又增其一。
value.en: Under the short reign of Emperor Zhao the court added only one more.
value.literal: Emperor Zhao had few undertakings, again added one thereof.

value.zh: 〈金城也。〉
value.en: 〈Jincheng commandery.〉
value.literal: 〈Jincheng.〉

value.zh: 至平帝元始二年，凡新置郡國七十有一，與秦四十，合一百一十有一。
value.en: By the second year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, Han had founded seventy-one new units; added to Qin's forty, the roster stood at one hundred eleven.
value.literal: Down to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year, in all newly established commanderies and kingdoms were seventy-one; together with Qin's forty, altogether one hundred eleven.

value.zh: 改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，又置徐州，復夏舊號，南置交阯，北有朔方，凡爲十三部。
value.en: Yong was changed to Liang, Liang to Yi; Xuzhou was further established; Xia's old designations were restored; Jiaozhi was set up in the south and Shuofang in the north—thirteen departments in all.
value.literal: Changed Yong to Liang, changed Liang to Yi, further established Xuzhou, restored Xia's old designations, south established Jiaozhi, north had Shuofang—in all became thirteen departments.

value.zh: 〈涼、益、荊、揚、青、豫、兗、徐、幽、并、冀十一州，交阯、朔方二刺史，合十三部。〉
value.en: 〈Eleven provinces from Liang to Ji plus two special zones, Jiaozhi and Shuofang, each with its own regional commissioner—thirteen departments in all.〉
value.literal: 〈Liang, Yi, Jing, Yang, Qing, Yu, Yan, Xu, You, Bing, Ji—eleven provinces; Jiaozhi, Shuofang—two regional inspectors; together thirteen departments.〉

value.zh: 光武投戈之歲，在彫秏之辰，郡國蕭條，并省者八。
value.en: When Guangwu laid down the sword, the realm was gaunt from war; eight redundant commanderies were folded away in the general retrenchment.
value.literal: In the year Guangwu cast aside the spear, it was a time of wasting exhaustion; commanderies and kingdoms were desolate; those merged and abolished were eight.

value.zh: 〈城陽、淄川、高密、膠東、六安、真定、泗水、廣陽。〉
value.en: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, and Guangyang were the eight struck from the map.〉
value.literal: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, Guangyang.〉

value.zh: 建武十一年，省州牧，復爲刺史，員十三人，各掌一州。
value.en: In the eleventh year of Jianwu the court abolished the provincial governorships, restored classic regional censors, and fixed their number at thirteen, one to each major province.
value.literal: Jianwu eleventh year, abolished provincial shepherds, again became censors; establishment thirteen men, each grasping one province.

value.zh: 明帝置一，
value.en: Emperor Ming added one seat,
value.literal: Mingdi established one,

value.zh: 〈永昌也。〉
value.en: 〈Yongchang in the far southwest.〉
value.literal: 〈Yongchang.〉

value.zh: 章帝置二，
value.en: Emperor Zhang added two commands,
value.literal: Zhangdi established two,

value.zh: 〈任城、吳郡。〉
value.en: 〈Rencheng and Wu commandery.〉
value.literal: 〈Rencheng, Wu commandery.〉

value.zh: 和順改作，其名有九。
value.en: Under Emperors He and Shun names were altered; there were nine of them.
value.literal: He and Shun altered and made; their names were nine.

value.zh: 〈和置濟北、廣陽，順改淮陽爲陳，改楚爲彭城，濟東爲東平，臨淮爲下邳，千乘爲六安，信都爲安平，天水爲漢陽。〉
value.en: 〈Emperor He revived Jibei and Guangyang; Emperor Shun renamed Huaiyang as Chen, the old Chu core as Pengcheng, Jidong as Dongping, Linhuai as Xiapi, Qiansheng as Liu'an, Xindu as Anping, and Tianshui as Hanyang.〉
value.literal: 〈He established Jibei and Guangyang; Shun changed Huaiyang to Chen, changed Chu to Pengcheng, Jidong to Dongping, Linhuai to Xiapi, Qiansheng to Liu'an, Xindu to Anping, Tianshui to Hanyang.〉

value.zh: 省朔方刺史，合之於司隸，凡十三部，
value.en: Shuofang's inspectorate was folded into the capital superintendent's zone, leaving thirteen departments in the Eastern Han scheme,
value.literal: Abolished the Shuofang regional inspector, merged it into the Metropolitan Superintendent; in all thirteen departments,

value.zh: 〈其與西漢不同者，司隸校尉部郡治河南，朔方隸於并部。〉
value.en: 〈Unlike Western Han, the metropolitan belt was administered from Henan, while Shuofang answered to the Bing inspector rather than standing alone.〉
value.literal: 〈Where it differs from Western Han: the Metropolitan Superintendent's commandery-administered region takes Henan as its seat; Shuofang is subordinate to Bing department.〉

value.zh: 而郡國百有八焉。
value.en: The Eastern Han roster thus held one hundred eight commanderies and kingdoms.
value.literal: And commanderies and kingdoms were one hundred eight.

value.zh: 〈省前漢八，分置五，改舊名七，因舊九十六，少前漢三也。〉
value.en: 〈Eight Western Han units were cut, five new ones split off, seven were simply renamed, ninety-six kept their old titles—three fewer than the old Han total.〉
value.literal: 〈Abolished eight of Former Han, split and established five, changed old names seven, continued old ninety-six—three fewer than Former Han.〉

value.zh: 桓靈頗增於前，復置六郡。
value.en: Under Emperors Huan and Ling the court added six commanderies beyond the earlier baseline.
value.literal: Huan and Ling somewhat increased over before, again established six commanderies.

value.zh: 〈桓，高陽、高涼、博陵；
value.en: 〈Emperor Huan created Gaoyang, Gaoliang, and Boling;
value.literal: 〈Huan: Gaoyang, Gaoliang, Boling;

value.zh: 靈，南安、鄱陽、廬陵。〉
value.en: Emperor Ling added Nan'an, Poyang, and Luling.〉
value.literal: Ling: Nan'an, Poyang, Luling.〉

value.zh: 魏武定霸，三方鼎立，生靈版蕩，關洛荒蕪，所置者十二，
value.en: When Wei Wu settled his hegemony, the three sides stood like a tripod, the people were thrown into turmoil, the passes and Luo region lay desolate, and those he established were twelve,
value.literal: Wei Wu settled hegemony; the three sides stood like a tripod; living beings were on tablet-like upheaval; Guan and Luo were desolate; those established were twelve,

value.zh: 〈新興、樂平、西平、新平、略陽、陰平、帶方、譙、樂陵、章武、南鄉、襄陽。〉
value.en: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, and Xiangyang.〉
value.literal: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, Xiangyang.〉

value.zh: 所省者七，
value.en: Seven older commands were struck at the same time,
value.literal: Those abolished were seven,

value.zh: 〈上郡、朔方、五原、雲中、定襄、漁陽、廬江。〉
value.en: 〈Shang, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, and Lujiang were the seven removed.〉
value.literal: 〈Shang commandery, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, Lujiang.〉

value.zh: 而文帝置七，
value.en: Emperor Wen of Wei then added seven more,
value.literal: And Wendi established seven,

value.zh: 〈朝歌、陽平、弋陽、魏興、新城、義陽、[2]安豐。〉
value.en: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉
value.literal: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉

value.zh: 明及少帝增二，
value.en: Emperor Ming and the first boy emperor each added one commandery—two in all,
value.literal: Ming and the Lesser Emperor added two,

value.zh: 〈明，上庸也；
value.en: 〈Mingdi restored Shangyong;
value.literal: 〈Ming: Shangyong;

value.zh: 少，平陽也。〉
value.en: the boy emperor added Pingyang.〉
value.literal: Lesser: Pingyang.〉

value.zh: 得漢郡者五十四焉。
value.en: Wei thus held fifty-four commanderies inherited from Han.
value.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were fifty-four.

value.zh: 蜀先主於漢建安之間初置郡九，
value.en: Between the Jian'an years, Liu Bei in Shu-Han first carved out nine commanderies,
value.literal: Shu's First Sovereign, in the interval of Han's Jian'an, first established nine commanderies,

value.zh: 〈巴東、巴西、梓潼、江陽、汶山、漢嘉、朱提、宕渠、涪陵。〉
value.en: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, and Fuling.〉
value.literal: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, Fuling.〉

value.zh: 後主增二，
value.en: Liu Shan later added two more,
value.literal: The Later Sovereign added two,

value.zh: 〈雲南、興古。〉
value.en: 〈Yunnan and Xingu in the far south.〉
value.literal: 〈Yunnan, Xingu.〉

value.zh: 得漢郡者十有一焉。
value.en: Shu ultimately held eleven Han-era commanderies.
value.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eleven.

value.zh: 吳主大皇帝初置郡五，
value.en: Sun Quan, Wu's Great Emperor, first founded five commanderies,
value.literal: The Wu ruler, the Great Emperor, first established five commanderies,

value.zh: 〈臨賀、武昌、珠崖、新安、廬陵南部。〉
value.en: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, and the southern annex of Luling.〉
value.literal: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, southern Luling.〉

value.zh: 少帝、景帝各四，
value.en: Sun Liang and Sun Xiu each added four commanderies,
value.literal: The Lesser Emperor and Emperor Jing each four,

value.zh: 〈少，臨川、臨海、衡陽、湘東。
value.en: 〈Sun Liang created Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, and Xiangdong;
value.literal: 〈Lesser: Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, Xiangdong.

value.zh: 景，天門、建安、建平、合浦北部。〉
value.en: Sun Xiu added Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, and northern Hepu.〉
value.literal: Jing: Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, northern Hepu.〉

value.zh: 歸命侯亦置十有二郡，
value.en: Sun Hao, the "Marquis Who Surrendered His Mandate," still ordered twelve more commanderies founded,
value.literal: The Marquis Who Submits to Fate also established twelve commanderies,

value.zh: 〈始安、始興、邵陵、安成、新昌、武平、九德、吳興、東陽、桂林、滎陽、宜都。〉
value.en: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, and Yidu.〉
value.literal: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, Yidu.〉

value.zh: 得漢郡者十有八焉。
value.en: Wu in the end controlled eighteen commanderies that had once belonged to Han.
value.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eighteen.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 吳孫休時，烏程人有得困病，及差，能以響言者，言于此而聞於彼。
value.en: During Sun Xiu's reign a Wucheng convalescent acquired ventriloquy that carried his voice miles from his lips.
value.literal: Under Wu's Sun Xiu, a man of Wucheng fell deathly ill; after he recovered he could "resounding-speak" — speak here and be heard there.

value.zh: 自其所聽之，不覺其聲之大也。
value.en: Beside him it sounded no louder than ordinary speech.
value.literal: From the listener's own place he did not notice the sound as particularly loud.

value.zh: 自遠聽之，如人對言，不覺聲之自遠來也。
value.en: From afar it seemed like conversation at arm's length, with no hint of distant projection.
value.literal: From a distance it was like face-to-face talk; one did not sense that the voice came from far away.

value.zh: 聲之所往，隨其所向，遠者所過十數里。
value.en: He could steer the voice through a dozen leagues or more.
value.literal: The sound went wherever he aimed it; those farthest heard it across more than ten li.

value.zh: 其鄰人有責息于外，歷年不還，乃假之使為責讓，懼以禍福。
value.en: A creditor used him to haunt a defaulter abroad with ghostly threats of blessing or woe.
value.literal: A neighbor had money lent abroad that went unreturned for years; he borrowed the gift to have him deliver rebukes, threatening fortune or calamity.

value.zh: 負物者以為鬼神，即傎倒畀之，其人亦不自知所以然也。
value.en: The frightened borrower paid in full at once, while the wonder-worker himself hardly grasped the trick.
value.literal: The debtor took it for a spirit, immediately turned everything over in payment; that man also did not know why it happened thus.

value.zh: 言不從之咎也。
value.en: The historians filed it under portents of distorted speech.
value.literal: This was a fault arising from words not following their proper course.

value.zh: 孫休永安二年，將守質子群聚嬉戲，有異小兒忽來言曰：「三公鋤，司馬如。」
value.en: Sun Xiu, Yong’an 2 — the hostage sons of the generals and garrison commanders had gathered to play when a strange child suddenly came and said, “The Three Dukes hoe; the Sima are like.”
value.literal: Sun Xiu, Yong’an 2 — the hostage sons of the generals and garrison commanders had gathered to play when a strange child suddenly came and said, “The Three Dukes hoe; the Sima are like.”

value.zh: 又曰：「我非人，熒惑星也。」
value.en: It also said: "I am not human — I am the Planet Mars."
value.literal: It also said: "I am not human — I am the Planet Mars."

value.zh: 言畢上升，仰視若曳一匹練，有頃沒。
value.en: The apparition shot upward like a comet and disappeared.
value.literal: Finishing, it rose into the sky; looking up it seemed to trail a bolt of silk; soon it vanished.

value.zh: 干寶曰：「後四年而蜀亡，六年而魏廢，二十一年而吳平。」
value.en: Gan Bao said: "Four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was cast off, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified."
value.literal: Gan Bao said: "Four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was cast off, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified."

value.zh: 於是九服歸晉。
value.en: The empire folded back under the Sima house.
value.literal: Thereupon the Nine Domains returned to Jin.

value.zh: 魏與吳蜀並戰國，「三公鋤，司馬如」之謂也。
value.en: Wei fought Wu and Shu as warring states — that is what "The three dukes hoe, the Sima like" meant.
value.literal: Wei fought Wu and Shu as warring states — that is what "The three dukes hoe, the Sima like" meant.

value.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳二年五月，陽羨縣離裏山大石自立。
value.en: In the fifth month of Wufeng 2 under Wu’s Sun Liang, a great stone at Lili Mountain stood upright on its own.
value.literal: Wu Sun Liang, Wufeng 2, fifth month — a great stone at Lili Mountain in Yangxian county stood upright by itself.

value.zh: 案京房《易傳》曰「庶士為天子之祥也」，其說曰：「石立於山同姓，平地異姓。」
value.en: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."
value.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."

value.zh: 干寶以為「孫皓承廢故之家得位，其應也。」
value.en: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."
value.literal: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."

value.zh: 或曰孫休見立之祥也。
value.en: Another reading favored Sun Xiu.
value.literal: Others say it signified Sun Xiu's enthronement.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
value.en: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
value.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.

value.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
value.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
value.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

value.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
value.en: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
value.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.

value.zh: 何不先謀之！」
value.en: Why not plot first!"
value.literal: Why not plot first!'

value.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
value.en: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
value.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.

value.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。
value.en: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
value.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

value.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
value.en: Lun was branded Jia's man.
value.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.

value.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
value.en: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
value.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.

value.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
value.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
value.en: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
value.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun assented.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
value.en: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
value.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.

value.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
value.en: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
value.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.

value.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。
value.en: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
value.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.

value.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。
value.en: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
value.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
value.en: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.
value.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

value.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
value.en: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
value.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.

value.zh: 時年二十三。
value.en: He died at twenty-three.
value.literal: He was twenty-three sui.

value.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。
value.en: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
value.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

value.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。
value.en: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
value.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

value.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
value.en: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
value.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.

value.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
value.en: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
value.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.

value.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」
value.en: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."
value.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'

value.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
value.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 禮志上
value.en: Rites Treatise, Part One
value.literal: Treatises on Rites, Part One

value.zh: 〈（案：《禮志序》，原本闕佚。）〉
value.en: (Editor's note: The preface to the Treatise on Rites is no longer extant in the original.)
value.literal: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Rites is missing from the original text.)

value.zh: 三年九月，將有事於南郊，議於東京別建太廟。
value.en: In the ninth month of the third year, with a southern-suburb sacrifice impending, officials deliberated building a separate imperial ancestral temple at the Eastern Capital.
value.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, when the southern suburb ceremony was to be performed, it was deliberated to separately build an imperial ancestral temple at the Eastern Capital.

value.zh: 時太常禮院言：「準洛京廟室一十五間，分為四室，東西各有夾室，四神門，每方屋一間，各三門，戟二十四，別有齋宮神廚屋宇。
value.en: The Court of Imperial Rites reported: "According to the Luoyang model, the temple comprises fifteen bays divided into four main chambers, with side chambers on east and west, four spirit gates, one bay per cardinal direction with three gates each, twenty-four halberds, and separate buildings for the fasting palace and spirit kitchen.
value.literal: At the time the Court of Imperial Rites said: "According to the Luoyang capital, the temple chambers number fifteen bays, divided into four chambers; east and west each have side chambers; four spirit gates; each direction has one bay with three gates each; twenty-four halberds; separately there are fasting-palace and spirit-kitchen buildings.

value.zh: 準禮，左宗廟，右社稷，在國城內，請下所司修奉。」
value.en: By rite the ancestral temple stands to the left and the altars of soil and grain to the right, within the capital walls; we request that the responsible offices be ordered to restore and maintain them."
value.literal: According to rites, the ancestral temple is to the left and the altars of soil and grain to the right, within the capital walls; we request dispatch to the relevant offices to restore and maintain them."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The proposal was approved.
value.literal: The request was granted.

value.zh: 其月，太常禮院奏：「迎太廟社稷神主到京，其日未審皇帝親出郊外迎奉否。
value.en: That same month, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "When the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain are brought to the capital, it remains undecided whether the emperor should personally go out beyond the city to receive them.
value.literal: That month, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "When welcoming the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain to the capital, it is not yet determined whether on that day the emperor will personally go out beyond the suburbs to receive them.

value.zh: 檢討故事，元無禮例，伏請召三省官集議。」
value.en: A search of precedents turns up no established ritual; we humbly request that officials of the Three Departments be convened to deliberate."
value.literal: Examining precedents, originally there is no ritual example; we humbly request summoning the Three Departments' officials to assemble and deliberate."

value.zh: 敕：「宜令尚書省四品以上、中書門下五品已上同參議。」
value.en: An edict ordered: "Officials of the fourth rank and above in the Secretariat, together with officials of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery, shall jointly deliberate."
value.literal: An edict: "It is fitting to order officials of the fourth rank and above in the Secretariat and of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery to participate jointly in deliberation."

value.zh: 司徒竇貞固、司空蘇禹珪等議：「按吳主孫休即位，迎祖父神主於吳郡，人祔太廟，前一日出城野次，明日常服奉迎，此其例也。」
value.en: Minister over the Masses Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works Su Yugui, and others argued: "When Sun Xiu of Wu took the throne, he welcomed his grandfather's spirit tablet from Wu Commandery for enshrinement in the ancestral temple; the day before he went out of the city and encamped in the open country, and the next day received the tablet in ordinary dress. That is the precedent."
value.literal: Minister over the Masses Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works Su Yugui, and others deliberated: "According to the precedent when Lord Sun Xiu of Wu acceded, he welcomed his grandfather's spirit tablet from Wu Commandery and had it enshrined in the imperial ancestral temple; the day before he went out of the city to encamp in the open country, and the next day in ordinary dress received and escorted it—this is the example."

value.zh: 遂署狀言車駕出城奉迎為是，請下禮儀使草定儀註。
value.en: They then signed a memorial recommending that the emperor go out of the city to receive the tablets, and requested that the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol draft the ceremonial regulations.
value.literal: Thereupon they signed a memorial stating that the imperial carriage going out of the city to receive and escort was correct, and requested dispatch to the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol to draft the ritual regulations.

value.zh: 至十月，禮儀使奏：「太祖神主將至，前一日儀仗出城掌次，於西禦莊東北設神主行廟幄幕，面南。
value.en: In the tenth month, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized: "When Taizu's spirit tablet is about to arrive, on the preceding day the guard of honor will go out of the city to prepare the encampment, and a traveling-temple canopy for the spirit tablet shall be erected northeast of the Western Imperial Estate, facing south.
value.literal: By the tenth month, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized: "When Taizu's spirit tablet is about to arrive, on the day before the guard of honor goes out of the city to manage the encampment, a traveling-temple canopy for the spirit tablet is set up northeast of the Western Imperial Estate, facing south.

value.zh: 其日放朝，群臣早出西門，皇帝常服出城詣行宮，群臣起居畢，就次。
value.en: On that day court is suspended; the officials assemble early at the Western Gate; the emperor goes out of the city in ordinary dress to the traveling palace; after the officials have paid their respects, they take their stations.
value.literal: On that day court is dismissed; the hundred officials go out early through the Western Gate; the emperor in ordinary dress goes out of the city to the traveling palace; when the hundred officials have finished paying respects, they take their places.

value.zh: 神主將至，群臣班定，皇帝立於班前。
value.en: As the spirit tablet approaches, the officials form their ranks and the emperor stands before them.
value.literal: When the spirit tablet is about to arrive, the hundred officials' ranks are set; the emperor stands before the ranks.

value.zh: 神主至，太常卿請皇帝再拜，群臣俱拜。
value.en: When the spirit tablet arrives, the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites asks the emperor to bow twice, and all the officials bow with him.
value.literal: When the spirit tablet arrives, the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites requests the emperor to bow twice; the hundred officials all bow.

value.zh: 神主就行廟幄幕座，設常饌，群臣班於神幄前。
value.en: The spirit tablet is conducted to its seat in the traveling-temple canopy; ordinary offerings are laid out, and the officials form ranks before the spirit canopy.
value.literal: The spirit tablet proceeds to the seat within the traveling-temple canopy; ordinary offerings are set out; the hundred officials rank before the spirit canopy.

value.zh: 侍中就次，請皇帝謁神主。
value.en: The Palace Attendant takes his station and asks the emperor to approach the spirit tablet.
value.literal: The Palace Attendant takes his place and requests the emperor to visit the spirit tablet.

value.zh: 既至，群臣再拜，皇帝進酒畢再拜，群臣俱拜。
value.en: When he arrives, the officials bow twice; after the emperor presents wine and bows again, all the officials bow with him.
value.literal: When he has arrived, the hundred officials bow twice; when the emperor has finished presenting wine he bows twice again; the hundred officials all bow.

value.zh: 皇帝還幄，群臣先赴太廟門外立班，俟皇帝至起居。
value.en: The emperor returns to the canopy; the officials go ahead to form ranks outside the ancestral temple gate and wait for the emperor to arrive and pay his respects.
value.literal: The emperor returns to the canopy; the hundred officials first go to stand in ranks outside the gate of the imperial ancestral temple, awaiting the emperor's arrival to pay respects.

value.zh: 俟神主至，群臣班於廟門外，皇帝立於班前，太常卿請皇帝再拜，群臣俱拜。
value.en: When the spirit tablet arrives, the officials form ranks outside the temple gate; the emperor stands before them; the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites asks the emperor to bow twice, and all the officials bow with him.
value.literal: Awaiting the spirit tablet's arrival, the hundred officials rank outside the temple gate; the emperor stands before the ranks; the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites requests the emperor to bow twice; the hundred officials all bow.

value.zh: 皇帝還幄，群臣就次，宮闈令安神主於本室訖，群臣班於廟庭。
value.en: The emperor returns to the canopy and the officials take their stations; the Director of the Inner Palace installs the spirit tablet in its proper chamber; when this is done, the officials form ranks in the temple courtyard.
value.literal: The emperor returns to the canopy; the hundred officials take their places; the Director of the Inner Palace installs the spirit tablet in its proper chamber; when finished, the hundred officials rank in the temple courtyard.

value.zh: 太常卿請皇帝於四室奠饗，逐室皇帝再拜，群臣俱拜。
value.en: The Director of the Court of Imperial Rites asks the emperor to offer sacrifice in each of the four chambers; at every chamber the emperor bows twice and all the officials bow with him.
value.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Rites requests the emperor to set out offerings and feast in the four chambers; at each chamber the emperor bows twice and the hundred officials all bow.

value.zh: 四室祔饗畢，皇帝還宮。
value.en: When the enshrinement offerings in all four chambers are complete, the emperor returns to the palace.
value.literal: When the enshrinement feasting in the four chambers is finished, the emperor returns to the palace.

value.zh: 前件儀註，望付中書門下宣下。」
value.en: We request that these ritual regulations be issued through the Secretariat and Chancellery."
value.literal: The foregoing ritual regulations are requested to be transmitted by the Secretariat and Chancellery for promulgation."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The proposal was approved.
value.literal: The request was granted.

value.zh: 霍峻字仲邈，南郡枝江人也。
value.en: Huo Jun, styled Zhongmiao, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.
value.literal: Huo Jun, courtesy name Zhongmiao, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

value.zh: 兄篤於鄉里合部曲數百人，篤卒，荊州牧劉表令峻攝其眾。
value.en: His older brother Huo Du had raised a few hundred local followers; after Du died, Jing governor Liu Biao put Jun in charge of that band.
value.literal: His elder brother Huo Du in the countryside assembled several hundred retainers in a private corps; when Du died, the Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, ordered Jun to take command of his troops.

value.zh: 表卒，峻率眾歸先主，先主以峻為中郎將。
value.en: After Liu Biao’s death, Jun brought his men to Liu Bei, who made him a general of the household.
value.literal: When Liu Biao died, Jun led the troops to submit to the First Sovereign, who appointed Jun General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

value.zh: 先主自葭萌南還襲劉璋，留峻守葭萌城。
value.en: Liu Bei marched south from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and left Huo Jun to hold the fortress there.
value.literal: The First Sovereign returned south from Jiameng to strike Liu Zhang, leaving Jun to defend Jiameng city.

value.zh: 張魯遣將楊帛誘峻，求共守城，峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得。」
value.en: Zhang Lu’s officer Yang Bo tried to win him over for a joint defense, but Huo Jun replied, "You may have my head; you will not have this city."
value.literal: Zhang Lu sent the general Yang Bo to entice Jun, seeking to defend the city together; Jun said, "This petty man's head may be taken, but the city cannot be taken."

value.zh: 帛乃退去。
value.en: Yang Bo withdrew his force.
value.literal: Bo thereupon withdrew.

value.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍攻峻，且一年，不能下。
value.en: Liu Zhang’s generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun then brought over ten thousand men up the Lang River and besieged the town for the better part of a year without breaking it.
value.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, attacked, besieged, and assaulted Jun for nearly a year but could not take him.

value.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，即斬存首。
value.en: Huo Jun had only a few hundred defenders. When he saw an opening, he sent picked troops out in a sortie, routed the besiegers, and took Xiang Cun’s head.
value.literal: Jun had only several hundred soldiers in the city; watching for their slackness and gaps, he selected crack troops, sallied out, struck them a great defeat, and beheaded Cun on the spot.

value.zh: 先主定蜀，嘉峻之功，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守、裨將軍。
value.en: Once Liu Bei had secured Shu, he singled out Huo Jun’s exploit, carved Zitong commandery out of Guanghan, and named him its governor with the rank of major general.
value.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, praised Jun's merit, thereupon divided Guanghan to make Zitong Commandery, and appointed Jun Administrator of Zitong and Major General.

value.zh: 在官三年，年四十卒，還葬成都。
value.en: He served three years in post, died at forty, and was brought home for burial in Chengdu.
value.literal: In office three years, at age forty he died; he was returned for burial at Chengdu.

value.zh: 先主甚悼惜，乃詔諸葛亮曰：「峻既佳士，加有功於國，欲行爵。」
value.en: The First Sovereign mourned him deeply and issued an edict to Zhuge Liang: "Jun was an excellent man and, moreover, had rendered merit to the state. I wish to grant him rank."
value.literal: The First Sovereign greatly mourned and pitied him, then issued an edict to Zhuge Liang saying, "Jun is already an excellent gentleman, moreover having merit for the state; I wish to carry out enfeoffment."

value.zh: 遂親率群僚臨會弔祭，因留宿墓上，當時榮之。
value.en: He then led the full court to the funeral, stayed the night by the grave, and contemporaries counted it the highest honor.
value.literal: Thereupon he personally led the host of officials to attend the assembly, mourn, and sacrifice, and on that account lodged overnight on the tomb; at the time they deemed it glorious.

value.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：罗宪字令则。
value.en: The Xiangyang ji gives Luo Xian’s style as Lingze.
value.literal: The Xiangyang ji states: Luo Xian, courtesy name Lingze.

value.zh: 父蒙，避乱於蜀，官至广汉太守。
value.en: His father Luo Meng had fled the turmoil into Shu and rose to governor of Guanghan.
value.literal: His father Meng, fleeing disorder, went to Shu, and his office reached Administrator of Guanghan.

value.zh: 宪少以才学知名，年十三能属文。
value.en: Even as a boy he was known for literary talent and could write polished essays at thirteen.
value.literal: Xian in youth was known for talent and learning; at thirteen sui he could compose texts.

value.zh: 后主立太子，为太子舍人，迁庶子、尚书吏部郎，以宣信校尉再使於吴，吴人称美焉。
value.en: After the crown prince was named, he served as gentleman attendant, then as palace attendant and personnel director at the secretariat, and twice went to Wu as envoy with the rank of colonel who spreads trust, winning praise in the eastern court.
value.literal: When the Later Sovereign established the heir apparent, he became gentleman attendant at the heir's palace, was promoted attendant and gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel of the Masters of Writing, and as Colonel Who Spreads Trust twice was sent on mission to Wu; the men of Wu praised him.

value.zh: 时黄皓预政，众多附之，宪独不与同，皓恚，左迁巴东太守。
value.en: When the eunuch Huang Hao dominated politics, most officials curried favor, but Luo Xian held aloof; Huang Hao exiled him to the governorship of Badong.
value.literal: At the time Huang Hao intervened in government, the multitude attached to him; Xian alone did not join with him; Hao was resentful and demoted him to Administrator of Badong.

value.zh: 时右大将军阎宇都督巴东，为领军，后主拜宪为宇副贰。
value.en: General Yan Yu of the right commanded east of Ba while also leading the central army; the emperor named Luo Xian his second-in-command there.
value.literal: At the time the General of the Right Yan Yu supervised Badong as commander-in-chief and was commander of the army; the Later Sovereign appointed Xian as Yu's deputy.

value.zh: 魏之伐蜀，召宇西还，留宇二千人，令宪守永安城。
value.en: When Wei invaded Shu, Yan Yu was recalled westward, leaving two thousand men under Luo Xian to hold Yong’an.
value.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, Yu was summoned to return west, two thousand of Yu's men were left, and Xian was ordered to defend Yong'an city.

value.zh: 寻闻成都败，城中扰动，江边长吏皆弃城走，宪斩称成都乱者一人，百姓乃定。
value.en: News of Chengdu’s fall threw the town into panic; riverfront magistrates bolted, but Luo Xian executed a man who spread false rumors of riot, and the people calmed down.
value.literal: Soon hearing of Chengdu's defeat, there was disturbance in the city; the senior officials along the river all abandoned the cities and fled; Xian beheaded one who claimed Chengdu was in chaos, and the hundred surnames then settled.

value.zh: 得后主委质问至，乃帅所统临于都亭三日。
value.en: When the emperor’s formal surrender order reached him, he led his troops to the metropolitan pavilion and kept mourning rites for three days.
value.literal: Having received the Later Sovereign's order to submit credentials, he thereupon led those he commanded to attend at the metropolitan pavilion three days.

value.zh: 吴闻蜀败，起兵西上，外讬救援，内欲袭宪。
value.en: Wu, learning of Shu’s collapse, marched west on the pretext of rescue while intending to seize Luo Xian’s position.
value.literal: Wu heard Shu was defeated, raised troops westward, outwardly pretending relief, inwardly wishing to strike Xian.

value.zh: 宪曰：“本朝倾覆，吴为脣齿，不恤我难而徼其利，背盟违约。
value.en: Luo Xian said, "My dynasty had fallen and Wu, supposedly a close ally, was profiting from Shu’s ruin instead of helping—breaking faith and the treaty.
value.literal: Xian said, "This court has overturned; Wu is lip and teeth; it does not pity our difficulty but seeks its profit, betraying the alliance and violating the covenant.

value.zh: 且汉已亡，吴何得久，宁能为吴降虏乎！”
value.en: Han was gone, he argued, and Wu could not last; he would never surrender to become Wu’s prisoner."
value.literal: Moreover Han is already gone; how can Wu long endure—how could I become a surrendered captive for Wu!

value.zh: 保城缮甲，告誓将士，厉以节义，莫不用命。
value.en: He strengthened the walls and arms, rallied his officers on their honor, and every man obeyed.
value.literal: He protected the city, repaired armor, announced oath to generals and soldiers, exhorted them with integrity and righteousness; none did not obey orders.

value.zh: 吴闻锺、邓败，百城无主，有兼蜀之志，而巴东固守，兵不得过，使步协率众而西。
value.en: After Zhong Hui and Deng Ai fell, Wu saw a chance to swallow Shu, but Luo Xian’s grip on Badong blocked the route, so Wu sent Bu Xie west with an army.
value.literal: Wu heard Zhong and Deng were defeated, a hundred cities had no master, and had the intention to annex Shu, but Badong firmly held and troops could not pass, so they sent Bu Xie to lead the host westward.

value.zh: 宪临江拒射，不能御，遣参军杨宗突围北出，告急安东将军陈骞，又送文武印绶、任子诣晋王。
value.en: Luo Xian’s bowmen along the river could not hold the line; he sent Yang Zong through the encirclement to Chen Qian and forwarded seals and hostages to the king of Jin.
value.literal: Xian along the river resisted with archery, could not withstand it, sent aide-de-camp Yang Zong to break the encirclement northward, report emergency to General Who Pacifies the East Chen Qian, and also sent civil and military seals and cords and hostage sons to the King of Jin.

value.zh: 协攻城，宪出与战，大破其军。
value.en: When Bu Xie assaulted the walls, Luo Xian sallied out and shattered his force.
value.literal: Xie attacked the city; Xian went out and fought with him, greatly smashing his army.

value.zh: 孙休怒，复遣陆抗等帅众三万人增宪之围。
value.en: Sun Xiu, furious, sent Lu Kang with thirty thousand more men to tighten the siege.
value.literal: Sun Xiu was angry and again sent Lu Kang and others to lead thirty thousand men to increase the siege of Xian.

value.zh: 被攻凡六月日而救援不到，城中疾病大半。
value.en: The siege ran half a year without relief, and disease laid low most of the garrison.
value.literal: Being attacked in all six months and relief not arriving, in the city sickness was more than half.

value.zh: 或说宪奔走之计，宪曰：“夫为人主，百姓所仰，危不能安，急而弃之，君子不为也，毕命於此矣。”
value.en: When someone urged retreat, he replied that a leader owed the people steadiness in danger; to bolt in a crisis was unworthy of a gentleman, and he would see the defense through here.
value.literal: Someone urged Xian on a plan of flight; Xian said, "Now as a people's lord, what the hundred surnames look up to, in peril unable to secure, in urgency abandoning them—a gentleman does not do this; I complete my life here."

value.zh: 陈骞言於晋王，遣荆州刺史胡烈救宪，抗等引退。
value.en: Chen Qian persuaded the king of Jin to send Hu Lie from Jingzhou; Lu Kang then lifted the siege.
value.literal: Chen Qian spoke to the King of Jin, who sent the Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie to rescue Xian; Kang and others drew back.

value.zh: 晋王即委前任，拜宪凌江将军，封万年亭侯。
value.en: The king confirmed him in office, named him general who crosses the river, and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Wannian.
value.literal: The King of Jin thereupon entrusted his former post, appointed Xian General Who Crosses the River, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wannian village.

value.zh: 会武陵四县举众叛吴，以宪为武陵太守巴东监军。
value.en: When four Wuling counties rose against Wu, he was appointed governor of Wuling and army supervisor for east of Ba.
value.literal: It happened that four counties of Wuling raised hosts and rebelled against Wu; Xian was made Administrator of Wuling and army supervisor of Badong.

value.zh: 泰始元年改封西鄂县侯。
value.en: In 265 his title was transferred to marquis of Xi'e county.
value.literal: In the first year of Taishi his fief was changed to Marquis of Xi'e county.

value.zh: 宪遣妻子居洛阳，武帝以子袭为给事中。
value.en: He moved his family to Luoyang, and Emperor Wu of Jin gave his son Luo Xi a post as palace attendant.
value.literal: Xian sent wife and children to dwell at Luoyang; Emperor Wu appointed his son Xi as palace attendant.

value.zh: 三年冬，入朝，进位冠军将军、假节。
value.en: In the winter of 267 he attended court and was promoted to general who vanquishes champions with ceremonial credentials.
value.literal: In the third year, winter, he entered court, was advanced in rank to General Who Vanquishes Champions, and granted credentials.

value.zh: 四年三月，从帝宴于华林园，诏问蜀大臣子弟，后问先辈宜时叙用者，宪荐蜀郡常忌、杜轸、寿良、巴西陈寿、南郡高轨、南阳吕雅、许国、江夏费恭、琅邪诸葛京、汝南陈裕，即皆叙用，咸显於世。
value.en: In the third month of the fourth year, he attended the emperor’s banquet in Hualin Park. An edict asked about the sons and younger brothers of Shu’s great ministers, and then about senior men of the previous generation who ought now to be appointed. Luo Xian recommended Chang Ji of Shu Commandery, Du Zhen, Shou Liang, Chen Shou of Baxi, Gao Gui of Nan Commandery, Lü Ya and Xu Guo of Nanyang, Fei Gong of Jiangxia, Zhuge Jing of Langye, and Chen Yu of Runan; all were appointed and all became prominent in their time.
value.literal: In the fourth year, third month, he followed the Emperor feasting in Hualin Garden; an edict asked about sons and younger brothers of Shu great ministers, afterward asking which elders of former times should be employed in due season; Xian recommended Chang Ji of Shu commandery, Du Zhen, Shou Liang, Chen Shou of Baxi, Gao Gui of Nan commandery, Lü Ya, Xu Guo, Fei Gong of Jiangxia, Zhuge Jing of Langye, Chen Yu of Runan; all were at once employed in order, all illustrious in the age.

value.zh: 宪还，袭取吴之巫城，因上伐吴之策。
value.en: When he came back he struck east, captured the Wu outpost at Wucheng, and followed with a memorial urging a campaign against Wu.
value.literal: Xian returned, raided and took Wu's Wucheng, and thereupon submitted a plan to attack Wu.

value.zh: 宪方亮严正，待士不倦，轻财好施，不治产业。
value.en: He was upright and austere, tireless with his men, generous with his purse, and uninterested in amassing property.
value.literal: Xian was square, bright, stern, and correct, treating gentlemen without weariness, lightening wealth and loving generosity, not managing estates.

value.zh: 六年薨，赠安南将军，谥曰烈侯。
value.en: He died in 270 and was posthumously named general who pacifies the south with the epithet “martial marquis.”
value.literal: In the sixth year he died; posthumously he was awarded General Who Pacifies the South, posthumous name Marquis Lie.

value.zh: 子袭，以凌江将军领部曲，早卒，追赠广汉太守。
value.en: His son Luo Xi, general who crosses the river leading family troops, died young and was honored posthumously as governor of Guanghan.
value.literal: The son Xi, as General Who Crosses the River leading retainers, died early; posthumously he was awarded Administrator of Guanghan.

value.zh: 袭子徽，顺阳内史，永嘉五年为王如所杀。
value.en: Luo Xi’s son Hui served as interior secretary of Shunyang and was killed by the rebel Wang Ru in 311.
value.literal: Xi's son Hui was interior secretary of Shunyang; in the fifth year of Yongjia he was killed by Wang Ru.

value.zh: 此作“献”，名与本传不同，未详孰是也。〉
value.en: The excerpt uses a different character for the name than our main text; it is unclear which spelling is right.〉
value.literal: Here the name is written with an alternate graph for xian, not matching this biography; which form is correct is unclear.〉

value.zh: 孫靜字幼臺，堅季弟也。
value.en: Sun Jing, styled Youtai, was the youngest of Sun Jian’s brothers.
value.literal: Sun Jing, courtesy name Youtai, was the youngest younger brother of Sun Jian.

value.zh: 堅始舉事，靜糾合鄉曲及宗室五六百人以為保障，眾咸附焉。
value.en: When Sun Jian first rose in arms, Sun Jing rallied some five or six hundred local men and kinsmen as a protective force, and people flocked to him.
value.literal: When Sun Jian first raised troops, Jing gathered five or six hundred men from the villages and the clan to serve as a safeguard, and the masses all attached themselves to him.

value.zh: 策破劉繇，定諸縣。
value.en: Sun Ce defeated Liu Yao and brought the counties under control.
value.literal: Ce defeated Liu Yao and pacified the various counties.

value.zh: 進攻會稽，遣人請靜，靜將家屬與策會於錢唐。
value.en: He pressed the attack on Kuaiji, sent for Sun Jing, and Sun Jing brought his household to join Sun Ce at Qiantang.
value.literal: Advancing to attack Kuaiji, he sent someone to summon Jing; Jing led his family members and met Ce at Qiantang.

value.zh: 是時太守王朗拒策於固陵，策數渡水戰，不能克。
value.en: The prefect Wang Lang held Sun Ce off at Guling; Sun Ce tried more than once to force a crossing and fight on the other bank but could not break through.
value.literal: At that time the Administrator Wang Lang resisted Ce at Guling; Ce several times crossed the water to give battle but could not overcome him.

value.zh: 靜說策曰："朗負阻城守，難可卒拔。
value.en: Sun Jing urged Sun Ce: Wang Lang is dug in behind natural barriers; you cannot expect to storm him overnight.
value.literal: Jing urged Ce, saying, Lang relies on natural obstacles and defends the city; he is hard to take in a hurry.

value.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，
value.en: Zha Creek lies a few dozen li to the south,
value.literal: Zha Creek is several tens of li south of here,

value.zh: 〈查音祖加反。〉
value.en: 〈The marginal gloss indicates that Zha takes its initial from zu and its rime from jia.〉
value.literal: 〈Note on pronunciation: the character for Zha is read zu-jia [fanqie].〉

value.zh: 而道之要徑也，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備、出其不意者也。
value.en: That route is the vital approach; thrust inland along it and strike where they do not expect you.
value.literal: and it is a crucial path; you ought to advance by that route and seize what lies within—what is called striking where they are unprepared and catching them unawares.

value.zh: 吾當自帥眾為軍前隊，破之必矣。
value.en: I will lead the main body myself as the first wave—we will crack them for certain.
value.literal: I shall personally lead the host as the vanguard of the army; we will surely break them.

value.zh: "策曰："善。
value.en: Sun Ce replied, Good.
value.literal: Ce said, Good.

value.zh: "乃詐令軍中曰："頃連雨水濁，兵飲之多腹痛，令促具罌缶數百口澄水。
value.en: Then he put out a false order: The river has been silty from all this rain; men who drink it are doubled up with cramps—have them ready hundreds of jars at once to draw off clear water.
value.literal: Then he falsely announced to the army: The rains have lately turned the water muddy; the soldiers drinking it have mostly gotten stomachaches—order them quickly to prepare several hundred jars and pots to settle the water.

value.zh: "至昏暮，羅以然火誑朗，便分軍夜投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。
value.en: At nightfall he lit decoy fires to fool Wang Lang, split his force, and marched up the Zha Creek track after dark to strike the camp at Gaoxian.
value.literal: At dusk he spread fires to deceive Lang, then divided the army and by night sent them along the Zha Creek road to raid the Gaoxian camp.

value.zh: 〈臣松之案：今永兴县有高迁桥。〉
value.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Gaoxian Bridge still stands in present-day Yongxing County.〉
value.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s investigation: today in Yongxing County there is a Gaoxian Bridge.〉

value.zh: 朗大驚。
value.en: Wang Lang was thrown into panic.
value.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed.

value.zh: 遣故丹楊太守周昕等帥兵前戰。
value.en: He dispatched the former Danyang prefect Zhou Xin and others to take the lead with their men.
value.literal: He sent the former Danyang Administrator Zhou Xin and others to lead troops forward into battle.

value.zh: 策破昕等，斬之，遂定會稽。
value.en: Sun Ce routed them, killed Zhou Xin, and settled Kuaiji.
value.literal: Ce defeated Xin and the others, beheaded them, and thereupon pacified Kuaiji.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昕字大明。
value.en: 〈According to the Kuaiji dianlu, Zhou Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji Canon Record states: Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.

value.zh: 少游京师，师事太傅陈蕃，博览群书，明於风角，善推灾异。
value.en: He had studied in the capital under Grand Tutor Chen Fan, read widely, and was adept at astrological signs and reading portents.
value.literal: In his youth he traveled to the capital and studied under Grand Tutor Chen Fan; he read widely and was skilled in “wind-angle” divination and interpreting anomalies.

value.zh: 辟太尉府，举高第，稍迁丹杨太守。
value.en: He entered the Grand Commandant’s service, graduated with highest honors, and rose step by step to prefect of Danyang.
value.literal: He was summoned to the Grand Commandant’s office, ranked at the top of his cohort, and was gradually promoted to Danyang Administrator.

value.zh: 曹公起义兵，昕前后遣兵万餘人助公征伐。
value.en: When Cao Cao raised his coalition army, Zhou Xin repeatedly sent him upward of ten thousand men for the campaigns.
value.literal: When Duke Cao raised the righteous army, Xin in succession sent more than ten thousand troops to assist the duke in his expeditions.

value.zh: 袁术之在淮南也，昕恶其淫虐，绝不与通。
value.en: While Yuan Shu occupied Huainan, Zhou Xin abhorred his cruelty and dissipation and would have nothing to do with him.
value.literal: When Yuan Shu was in Huainan, Xin detested his debauchery and cruelty and utterly refused dealings with him.

value.zh: 献帝春秋曰：袁术遣吴景攻昕，未拔，景乃募百姓敢从周昕者死不赦。
value.en: The Xiandi Chunqiu records that Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing against Zhou Xin without reducing him; Wu Jing then threatened the populace that anyone who sided with Zhou Xin would die without mercy.
value.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing to attack Xin but did not capture him; Jing then promised the common people that whoever dared follow Zhou Xin would be put to death without pardon.

value.zh: 昕曰：“我则不德，百姓何罪？”
value.en: Zhou Xin said, If I am the one at fault, what have the people done wrong?
value.literal: Xin said, If I lack virtue, what crime have the common people committed?

value.zh: 遂散兵，还本郡。〉
value.en: So he sent his soldiers home and withdrew to his own commandery.
value.literal: Thereupon he dispersed his troops and returned to his native commandery.

value.zh: 表拜靜為奮武校尉，欲授之重任，靜戀墳墓宗族，不樂出仕，求留鎮守。
value.en: Sun Ce recommended him as Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might and meant to give him a major post, but Sun Jing was unwilling to leave his family graves and kin and asked instead to stay and hold the territory.
value.literal: [Sun Ce] memorialized and appointed Jing Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might, wishing to give him heavy responsibility; Jing was attached to his ancestral graves and clan and did not relish leaving office, and asked to remain to guard and hold the region.

value.zh: 策從之。
value.en: Sun Ce agreed.
value.literal: Ce granted his request.

value.zh: 權統事，就遷昭義中郎將，終於家。
value.en: When Sun Quan took charge, Sun Jing was promoted in place to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and ended his days at home.
value.literal: When Quan assumed direction of affairs, [Jing] was promoted on the spot to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and died at home.

value.zh: 有五子，皓、瑜、皎、奐、謙。
value.en: He had five sons—Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.
value.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.

value.zh: 皓三子：綽、超、恭。
value.en: Sun Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.
value.literal: Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.

value.zh: 超為偏將軍。
value.en: Sun Chao rose to General of the Left.
value.literal: Chao served as General of the Left.

value.zh: 恭生峻。
value.en: Sun Gong was the father of Sun Jun.
value.literal: Gong fathered Jun.

value.zh: 綽生綝。
value.en: Sun Chuo was the father of Sun Lin.
value.literal: Chuo fathered Lin.

value.zh: 子泰，曹氏之甥也，為長水校尉。
value.en: His son Sun Tai was a Cao in-law and rose to colonel of Changan waters.
value.literal: His son Tai was the Cao clan's nephew by marriage and served as Colonel of Changan Waters.

value.zh: 嘉禾三年，從權圍新城，中流矢死。
value.en: In Jiahe 3 he joined Sun Quan’s siege of Xincheng and died to a stray shaft.
value.literal: In the third year of Jiahe he followed Quan in besieging Xincheng and was struck by a stray arrow and died.

value.zh: 泰子秀為前將軍、夏口督。
value.en: Sun Tai’s son Sun Xiu was General of the Van and commander at Xiakou.
value.literal: Tai's son Xiu was General of the Van and inspector of Xiakou.

value.zh: 秀公室至親，握兵在外，皓意不能平。
value.en: Sun Xiu was imperial kin commanding troops on the frontier—Sun Hao could not abide it.
value.literal: Xiu was closest kin of the ducal house and held troops abroad—Hao could not stomach it.

value.zh: 建衡二年，皓遣何定將五千人至夏口獵。
value.en: In Jianheng 2 Sun Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt near Xiakou.
value.literal: In the second year of Jianheng Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt at Xiakou.

value.zh: 先是，民間歛言秀當見圖，而定遠獵，秀遂驚，夜將妻子親兵數百人奔晉。
value.en: Rumors already said Sun Xiu would be framed; when He Ding ranged far afield on “hunt,” Sun Xiu bolted by night with family and hundreds of guards into Jin.
value.literal: Before this, folk rumor said Xiu would be plotted against; Ding hunted far away—Xiu was alarmed and by night led wife, children, and several hundred household guards to flee to Jin.

value.zh: 晉以秀為驃騎將軍、儀同三司，封會稽公。
value.en: Jin named him general of agile cavalry with Three Ducal honors and duke of Kuaiji.
value.literal: Jin appointed Xiu General of Agile Cavalry with ceremonies equal to the Three Offices and enfeoffed him Duke of Kuaiji.

value.zh: 〈江表传曰：皓大怒，追改秀姓曰厉。
value.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan: Sun Hao was so enraged he renamed Sun Xiu “Li” retroactively.)
value.literal: 〈《Jiangbiao zhuan》 states: Hao was furious and retroactively changed Xiu's surname to Li.

value.zh: 干宝《晋纪》曰：秀在晋朝，初闻皓降，群臣毕贺，秀称疾不与，南向流涕曰：“昔讨逆弱冠以一校尉创业，今后主举江南而弃之，宗庙山陵，於此为墟。
value.en: Gan Bao’s Jin ji: at the Jin court, when word came that Sun Hao had yielded, ministers rejoiced while Sun Xiu stayed away ill, faced south, and wept: “The Marshal Who Attacks Rebels began at twenty with a colonel’s commission; our last lord threw away the south—the ancestral shrines lie in dust.
value.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Ji states: When Xiu was at the Jin court, he first heard Hao had surrendered; the ministers all congratulated—Xiu claimed illness and did not attend; facing south he wept and said, “Formerly the Marshal Who Attacks Rebels at twenty founded the realm with a colonel's rank; now the Later Lord raises Jiangnan yet casts it away—the ancestral temples and imperial tombs lie in ruins here.

value.zh: 悠悠苍天，此何人哉！”
value.en: O vast Heaven—what men have brought us here!”
value.literal: Vast heaven—what manner of men are these!”

value.zh: 朝廷美之。
value.en: The Jin court praised him.
value.literal: The court praised him.

value.zh: 晋诸公赞曰：吴平，降为伏波将军，开府如故。
value.en: (The Jin zhugong zan: after Wu fell he was demoted to general who calms the waves but kept his staff.)
value.literal: 《Jin zhugong zan》 states: When Wu was pacified, he was reduced to General Who Calms the Waves with offices as before.

value.zh: 永宁中卒，追赠骠骑、开府。
value.en: He died under Yongning and was posthumously honored as agile cavalry general with full offices.
value.literal: He died during Yongning; posthumously honored Agile Cavalry with offices.

value.zh: 子俭，字仲节，给事中。〉
value.en: His son Sun Jian, styled Zhongjie, served as palace attendant.〉
value.literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Zhongjie, served as attendant within.〉

value.zh: 韶年十七，收河餘眾，繕治京城。
value.en: At seventeen Sun Shao rallied Sun He’s troops and rebuilt Jingcheng.
value.literal: At age seventeen Shao gathered He's remaining host, repaired and ordered Jingcheng.

value.zh: 起樓櫓，修器備議禦敵。
value.en: He raised watchtowers, stocked weapons, and prepared a defense.
value.literal: He raised towered engines, repaired implements and equipment, and laid plans to resist the enemy.

value.zh: 權聞亂，從椒丘還，過定丹楊，引軍歸吳。
value.en: Hearing of the revolt, Sun Quan raced back from Jiaoqiu, secured Danyang on the way, and marched for Wu.
value.literal: When Quan heard of the disturbance he returned from Jiaoqiu, pacified Danyang en route, and led the army back to Wu.

value.zh: 夜至京城下營，試攻驚之，兵皆乘城傳檄備警，歡聲動地，頗射外人，權使曉喻乃止。
value.en: He camped under Jingcheng by night and feinted an assault—the garrison manned the walls, passed orders, cheered till the ground shook, and peppered the darkness with arrows until Sun Quan explained himself at dawn.
value.literal: By night he camped below Jingcheng and probed with a trial attack to startle them—the troops all mounted the walls, passed writs and stood alert; joyous shouts shook the earth; they shot rather freely at those outside; Quan sent word of dawn before they stopped.

value.zh: 明日見韶，甚器之。
value.en: Next morning he met Sun Shao and was deeply impressed.
value.literal: The next day he saw Shao and greatly esteemed him.

value.zh: 即拜承烈校尉，統河部曲，食曲阿、丹徒二縣，自置長吏，一如河舊。
value.en: He named him Colonel Who Upholds Fierce Resolve over Sun He’s old troops, with revenue from Qu’e and Dantu and the same right to pick county magistrates.
value.literal: He immediately appointed him Colonel Who Upholds Fierce Resolve, commanding He's troops, subsisting on Qu’e and Dantu counties, appointing his own magistrates—exactly as He had formerly done.

value.zh: 後為廣陵太守、偏將軍。
value.en: Later he was Guangling prefect and General of the Left.
value.literal: Later he became Administrator of Guangling and General of the Left.

value.zh: 權為吳王，遷揚威將軍，封建德侯。
value.en: When Sun Quan took the Wu kingship Sun Shao became General Who Displays Might and marquis of Jiande.
value.literal: When Quan became King of Wu he promoted him General Who Displays Might and enfeoffed him Marquis of Jiande.

value.zh: 權稱尊號，為鎮北將軍。
value.en: When Sun Quan declared himself emperor Sun Shao was named General Who Guards the North.
value.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title he became General Who Guards the North.

value.zh: 韶為邊將數十年，善養士卒，得其死力。
value.en: For decades on the frontier he fed his men well and earned their lives.
value.literal: Shao was a frontier general several decades; he was good at nurturing soldiers and won their willingness to die.

value.zh: 常以警疆場遠斥候為務，先知動靜而為之備，故鮮有負敗。
value.en: He lived on alert patrols, learned enemy moves early, and seldom lost.
value.literal: He constantly took warning the borderlands and scouting far as his task; knowing enemy movements beforehand he prepared—therefore he rarely suffered defeat.

value.zh: 青、徐、汝、沛頗來歸附，淮南濱江屯候皆徹兵遠徙，徐、泗、江、淮之地，不居者各數百里。
value.en: People from Qing, Xu, Ru, and Pei drifted south; Wei stripped its Huai River posts—hundreds of li along Xu-Si-Jiang-Huai stood empty.
value.literal: Qing, Xu, Ru, and Pei largely came to submit; Huainan riverbank watch posts all withdrew troops and moved far—along Xu, Si, Jiang, and Huai unsettled lands stretched several hundred li each.

value.zh: 自權西征，還都武昌，韶不進見者十餘年。
value.en: After Sun Quan marched west and fixed his court at Wuchang, Sun Shao stayed away from audience for more than ten years.
value.literal: From Quan's western expedition and return capital to Wuchang, Shao did not advance to audience for over ten years.

value.zh: 權還建業，乃得朝覲。
value.en: Only when Sun Quan moved back to Jianye did Sun Shao appear at court.
value.literal: When Quan returned to Jianye he was then able to pay court visit.

value.zh: 權問青、徐諸屯要害，遠近人馬眾寡，魏將帥姓名，盡具識之，有問鹹對。
value.en: Sun Quan quizzed him on Qing-Xu strongpoints, troop counts, distances, Wei commanders—Sun Shao answered every question from memory.
value.literal: Quan asked about the critical points of the various garrisons in Qing and Xu, the distance and numbers of men and horses, and the names of Wei generals—he knew them all completely; whatever was asked he answered.

value.zh: 身長八尺，儀貌都雅。
value.en: He stood eight chi, composed and handsome.
value.literal: His body was eight chi tall; his bearing was refined.

value.zh: 權歡悅曰："吾久不見公禮，不圖進益乃爾。
value.en: Sun Quan said with delight: I have missed you so long—I never guessed you had grown this sharp.
value.literal: Quan joyfully said: I have long not seen Gongli—I did not imagine your advance could be thus.

value.zh: "加領幽州牧、假節。
value.en: He added him as inspector of You province with ceremonial axe and staff.
value.literal: He additionally appointed Inspector of You Province and granted the tally of authority.

value.zh: 赤烏四年卒。
value.en: He died in Chiwu 4.
value.literal: He died in the fourth year of Chiwu.

value.zh: 子越嗣，至右將軍，越兄楷武衛大將軍、臨成侯，代越為京下督。
value.en: His son Sun Yue inherited and rose to General of the Right; elder brother Sun Kai was grand marshal of the martial guard and marquis of Lincheng, replacing Sun Yue as capital-zone commander.
value.literal: His son Yue succeeded; he rose to General of the Right; Yue's elder brother Kai was grand marshal of the martial guard and Marquis of Lincheng, replacing Yue as commander below the capital.

value.zh: 楷弟異至領軍將軍，奕宗正卿，恢武陵太守。
value.en: Sun Kai's younger brother became commanding general of the household army; a second Sun Yi headed the ministry for the imperial clan; Sun Hui was prefect of Wuling.
value.literal: Kai's younger brother Yi rose to General Who Commands the Army; Yi became minister of the imperial clan; Hui was Administrator of Wuling.
