value.zh: 天璽元年，征楷為宮下鎮驃騎將軍。
value.en: In Tianxi 1 Sun Kai was summoned as palace agile-cavalry general.
value.literal: In the first year of Tianxi Kai was summoned as agile-cavalry general below the palace.

value.zh: 初永安賊施但等劫皓弟謙，襲建業，或白楷二端不即赴討者，皓數遣詰楷。
value.en: When Yong’an rebels seized Sun Hao’s brother Sun Qian and struck Jianye, rumor said Sun Kai hesitated—Sun Hao berated him again and again.
value.literal: At first the Yong’an bandits Shi Dan and others kidnapped Hao's younger brother Qian and raided Jianye; someone reported Kai wavered and did not immediately march to punish them—Hao repeatedly sent to rebuke Kai.

value.zh: 楷常惶怖，而卒被召，遂將妻子親兵數百人歸晉，晉以為車騎將軍，封丹楊侯。
value.en: Living in dread, Sun Kai bolted to Jin with family and hundreds of guards when summoned; Jin named him chariots-and-cavalry general and marquis of Danyang.
value.literal: Kai was constantly fearful; when he was finally summoned he therefore led wife, children, and several hundred household guards to return to Jin—Jin appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed him Marquis of Danyang.

value.zh: 〈晋诸公赞曰：吴平，降为渡辽将军，永安元年卒。
value.en: 〈The Jin zhugong zan: after Wu fell he became general who crosses the Liao and died in Yongan 1.)
value.literal: 〈《Jin zhugong zan》 states: When Wu was pacified he was reduced to General Who Crosses the Liao and died in the first year of Yongan.

value.zh: 吴录曰：楷处事严整不如孙秀，而人间知名，过也。〉
value.en: (The Wu lu says Sun Kai ran a looser ship than Sun Xiu yet was more famous—odd praise.〉
value.literal: 《Wu lu》 states: Kai's handling of affairs was less rigorous than Sun Xiu's, yet he was better known among people—this surpassed reason.〉

value.zh: 張昭字子布，彭城人也。
value.en: Zhang Zhao, styled Zibu, hailed from Pengcheng.
value.literal: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Zibu, was a man of Pengcheng.

value.zh: 少好學，善隸書，從白侯子安受《左氏春秋》，博覽眾書，與琅邪趙昱、東海王朗俱發名友善。
value.en: As a youth he loved books, wrote a fine clerical hand, studied the Zuo commentary under Bai Hou Zi’an, read omnivorously, and made his name alongside Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai.
value.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at clerical script, received Zuo's Spring and Autumn from Bai Hou Zi'an, read widely among texts, and together with Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai rose to fame as friendly associates.

value.zh: 弱冠察孝廉，不就。
value.en: Recommended as filially pious and incorrupt at his capping, he refused appointment.
value.literal: At the capping age he was investigated as filially pious and incorrupt but did not take office.

value.zh: 與朗共論舊君諱事，州裡才士陳琳等皆稱善之。
value.en: He argued with Wang Lang over taboos for former rulers; local talents such as Chen Lin praised his performance.
value.literal: Together with Lang he debated the affair of tabooing former lords; talented men of the commandery such as Chen Lin all praised them.

value.zh: 〈时汝南主簿应劭议宜为旧君讳，论者皆互有异同，事在《风俗通》。
value.en: 〈Ying Shao of Runan had argued for tabooing former masters; the dispute is recorded in the Fengsu tong.)
value.literal: 〈At that time Ying Shao, chief clerk of Runan, argued one ought taboo former lords; debaters differed from one another—the affair is in Fengsu tong.

value.zh: 昭著论曰：“客有见大国之议，士君子之论，云起元建武已来，旧君名讳五十六人，以为后生不得协也。
value.en: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A certain visitor had examined the debates of a great state and the arguments of learned gentlemen. He said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later generations could no longer use names with the same sounds.
value.literal: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A guest had seen the deliberations of a great state and the discussions of gentlemen, and said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty, there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later-born people could not use matching sounds.

value.zh: 取乎经论，譬诸行事，义高辞丽，甚可嘉羡。
value.en: Drawn from canonical gloss and matched to precedent, the rhetoric glows—yet something troubles me.
value.literal: Taking from the classics and commentaries, comparing to deeds performed, the righteousness is lofty and phrases lovely—greatly to be admired.

value.zh: 愚意褊浅，窃有疑焉。
value.en: Forgive a shallow mind—I cannot quite agree.
value.literal: My foolish thought is narrow and shallow—I privately harbor doubt.

value.zh: 盖乾坤剖分，万物定形，肇有父子君臣之经。
value.en: Once heaven and earth divided and creation took shape, the bonds of parent and child, ruler and subject, appeared.
value.literal: In general when Heaven and Earth split apart and the myriad things fixed their forms, there began the constant pattern of father and son, lord and minister.

value.zh: 故圣人顺天之性，制礼尚敬，在三之义，君实食之，在丧之哀，君亲临之，厚莫重焉，恩莫大焉，诚臣子所尊仰，万夫所天恃，焉得而同之哉？
value.en: The sage fashioned ritual from heaven’s nature: lords feed us under the “three that endure”; they mourn with us—nothing outweighs that debt. How can subjects rank them with ordinary kin?
value.literal: Therefore the sage complies with heaven's nature, institutes ritual and esteems reverence; in the duty of the three the lord truly nourishes; in mourning's grief the lord personally attends—the thickness cannot be heavier, the grace cannot be greater—truly what ministers and sons revere and myriad men rely on—how can they be equated?

value.zh: 然亲亲有衰，尊尊有杀，故礼服上不尽高祖，下不尽玄孙。
value.en: Yet kinship weakens by generation and mourning scales down—hence hemp stops short of the fifth grandfather above and the fifth grandson below.
value.literal: Yet intimacy toward kin has degrees of decline; reverence toward superiors has steps of reduction—therefore mourning garments upward do not exhaust great-great-grandfather, downward do not exhaust great-great-grandchild.

value.zh: 又传记四世而缌麻，服之穷也；
value.en: Genealogies say after four generations one wears only thin hemp.
value.literal: Moreover transmitted records: four generations and thin hemp—end of garments;

value.zh: 五世袒免，降杀同姓也；
value.en: After five generations one merely bares head and wrist—the mourning grade fades even within the clan.
value.literal: five generations shed turban and fringe—reduced severity toward same surname;

value.zh: 六世而亲属竭矣。
value.en: By the sixth generation kinship ends.
value.literal: six generations and kinship ties are exhausted.

value.zh: 又曲礼有不逮事之义则不讳，不讳者，盖名之谓，属绝之义，不拘於协，况乃古君五十六哉！
value.en: The Summary of Etiquette also exempts those who never served a lord from tabooing him—that ends obligation to a mere name. If distant kin need not rhyme away syllables, why taboo scores of dead kings?
value.literal: Moreover the Summary of Etiquette has the sense that if one did not succeed to service there is no taboo—no taboo refers to personal names; meaning of severed connection is not bound by harmonizing—how much more fifty-six ancient lords!

value.zh: 邾子会盟，季友来归，不称其名，咸书字者，是时鲁人嘉之也。
value.en: When the Zhu ruler met allies and Jiyou came home, the classic wrote his style, not his name—Lu admired the tact.
value.literal: The lord of Zhu at covenant assembly, Jiyou came to return—his name was not called; all were written with style—at that time the people of Lu praised it.

value.zh: 何解臣子为君父讳乎？
value.en: So why insist clerks taboo every syllable of old patrons?
value.literal: How explain ministers and sons tabooing for lord and father?

value.zh: 周穆王讳满，至定王时有王孙满者，其为大夫，是臣协君也。
value.en: Zhou King Mu banned “Man,” yet under King Ding a minister Wangsun Man served—a subject bore the sovereign’s taboo.
value.literal: King Mu of Zhou tabooed Man; when it reached King Ding there was Wangsun Man who was grand officer—that is a minister harmonizing with his lord.

value.zh: 又厉王讳胡，及庄王之子名胡，其比众多。
value.en: King Li banned “Hu,” yet Zhuang’s son was Hu—examples abound.
value.literal: Moreover King Li tabooed Hu; and among King Zhuang's sons one was named Hu—their parallels are numerous.

value.zh: 夫类事建议，经有明据，传有徵案，然后进攻退守，万无奔北，垂示百世，永无咎失。
value.en: Advice must rest on canonical proof and commentary precedent—otherwise posterity laughs.
value.literal: When grouping affairs and proposing counsel, the classics have clear proofs and the commentaries verifiable cases—then advancing attack or retreating defense never flees north in defeat; displaying for a hundred generations, never failing or missing.

value.zh: 今应劭虽上尊旧君之名，而下无所断齐，犹归之疑云。
value.en: Ying Shao honors old masters’ names yet sets no clear rule below—it stays muddled.
value.literal: Now although Ying Shao upward honors former lords' names, downward he decides nothing uniform—still it returns to doubtful clouds.

value.zh: 曲礼之篇，疑事无质，观省上下，阙义自证，文辞可为，倡而不法，将来何观？
value.en: The Summary of Etiquette passages he cites prove nothing; pretty words without law teach nothing.
value.literal: The Summary of Etiquette chapter—doubtful matters lack substance; observing above and below, missing righteousness proves itself—literary phrasing may be composed, advocated but not lawful—what will the future behold?

value.zh: 言声一放，犹拾瀋也，过辞在前，悔其何追！”〉
value.en: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉
value.literal: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉

value.zh: 刺史陶謙舉茂才，不應，謙以為輕己，遂見拘執。
value.en: Prefect Tao Qian nominated him for office; when Zhang Zhao declined, Tao felt insulted and jailed him.
value.literal: Inspector Tao Qian nominated him outstanding talent; he did not respond—Qian thought he slighted himself and thereupon had him seized.

value.zh: 昱傾身營救，方以得免。
value.en: Zhao Yu spent himself on bail until Zhang Zhao went free.
value.literal: Yu threw himself into arranging rescue—only then did he obtain release.

value.zh: 漢末大亂，徐方士民多避難揚土，昭皆南渡江。
value.en: Late Han turmoil drove Xu refugees south—Zhang Zhao crossed with them.
value.literal: At the end of Han great chaos arose; gentlemen and commoners of Xu region mostly fled calamity to Yang territory—Zhao all crossed the river south.

value.zh: 孫策創業，命昭為長史、撫軍中郎將，升堂拜母，如比肩之舊，文武之事，一以委昭。
value.en: Sun Ce named him chief clerk and general who pacifies the army, treated him like family before Lady Wu, and handed him every civil and military file.
value.literal: When Sun Ce founded the enterprise he appointed Zhao chief clerk and General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the Army, ascended the hall to bow to his mother as with old peers shoulder to shoulder—civil and military affairs he wholly entrusted to Zhao.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：策得昭甚悦，谓曰：“吾方有事四方，以士人贤者上，吾於子不得轻矣。”
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Ce rejoiced: I mean to stride the empire—among scholar-advisers I must honor you.
value.literal: [Wu shu] states: Ce gained Zhao and was very pleased, saying to him: I am about to have affairs in the four quarters—with scholar worthies above I cannot treat you lightly.

value.zh: 乃上为校尉，待以师友之礼。〉
value.en: So he raised him to colonel and courted him as mentor.
value.literal: Thereupon he promoted him to colonel and treated him with the ritual of teacher and friend.

value.zh: 昭每得北方士大夫書疏，專歸美於昭，昭欲嘿而不宣則懼有私，宣之則恐非宜，進退不安。
value.en: Northern letters flattered Zhang Zhao alone; silence seemed sneaky, publication awkward—he squirmed either way.
value.literal: Whenever Zhao obtained letters from northern gentlemen-officials they exclusively attributed praise to Zhao; Zhao wished to keep silent and not announce yet feared there was partiality; announcing yet feared it was not appropriate—advancing and retreating were uneasy.

value.zh: 策聞之，歡笑曰："昔管仲相齊，一則仲父，二則仲父，而桓公為霸者宗。
value.en: Sun Ce laughed: Guan Zhong called Huan Gong Father twice—and Huan became hegemon.
value.literal: When Ce heard it he laughed happily and said: Formerly Guan Zhong served Qi—first 'Father Zhong,' second 'Father Zhong,' yet Duke Huan became hegemon-in-chief.

value.zh: 今子布賢，我能用之，其功名獨不在我乎!"，
value.en: Zibu is worthy; if I use him well, the glory is surely mine!
value.literal: Now Zibu is worthy—if I can employ him, will the merit and fame alone not rest with me!"

value.zh: 周昭者字恭遠，與韋曜、薛瑩、華核並述《吳書》，後為中書郎，坐事下獄，核表救之，孫休不聽，遂伏法雲。
value.en: Zhou Zhao, courtesy name Gongyuan, helped Wei Yao, Xue Ying, and Hua He compile the Wu shu, later served as a palace secretariat officer, was jailed for an offense; Hua He appealed for him but Emperor Xiu of Wu refused, and Zhao was put to death.
value.literal: Zhou Zhao styled Gongyuan—with Wei Yao, Xue Ying, Hua He together composed Wu shu—later became Palace Secretariat gentleman—sat affair lower prison—He submitted memorial rescue him—Sun Xiu not listened—thereby executed law.

value.zh: 虞翻字仲翔，會稽餘姚人也。
value.en: Yu Fan, styled Zhongxiang, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.
value.literal: Yu Fan, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻少好学，有高气。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that as a young man Yu Fan loved scholarship and carried himself with uncommon elevation.
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: In youth Fan loved learning and bore himself with lofty pride.
